evidence.observation: Shared local guard for metadata operations (listTeams, listTasks). When a selector field is absent/blank it throws ParamError synchronously, so malformed requests fail as a typed local error and never reach the HTTP transport where a raw response shape could leak.

Team listing overloads build the payload through body(...) and then call requireAnyString(payload, ['user_id','user_key'], 'listTeams'); calling listTeams({}) therefore rejects with ParamError instead of issuing a request that returns an unvalidated envelope.

ACL permission-check metadata operation. It delegates to this.http.post and returns PermCheckResult on success; on any remote failure the injected transport converts the response into a normalized TDAMError, so the caller never observes a raw HTTP/envelope object.

The class overloads its constructor to accept either a config or an injected Transport ('post' in configOrTransport). That seam lets the failure contract drive the real normalization path deterministically with a stubbed fetch, without changing production code.

The single normalization point for metadata calls: non-JSON bodies become TDAMError(code=status|-1), and any envelope with code!==0 or a non-2xx status is rejected as TDAMError(code, message, requestId, details). It always throws the typed error class rather than returning/ rejecting with the Response or parsed envelope.

Typed remote-failure class carrying code, requestId and optional normalized details; message is formatted as '[code] message (request_id=...)'. This is the shape callers receive instead of a raw response shape.
Typed local-validation failure (extends TypeError, name='ParamError') thrown by the metadata client's own guards before any network call.

claims.claim: MetadataClient.checkAcl surfaces a remote failure as a normalized TDAMError (name 'TDAMError', numeric code, formatted message, requestId), never as a Response or a raw parsed envelope: an HTTP 200 body {code:40001,message:'acl denied',request_id:'body-req-1'} yields code 40001, the server message and the envelope request_id, with no leaked `data` field.

The metadata client's local guards (body/requireAnyString) fail fast with ParamError before any HTTP call: listTeams({}) and listTasks({}) throw synchronously, and a fetch spy records zero calls, so bad input can never leak an unvalidated response shape.

Non-JSON transport failures are still typed: an HTTP 503 body 'upstream boom' becomes TDAMError code 503 with the body text in message and the requestId taken from the x-qcloud-transaction-id header, and a 200 OK non-JSON body becomes TDAMError code -1.

MetadataClient injects a Transport via its overloaded constructor, which is the seam the executable contract uses to exercise the real V3HttpTransport normalization path deterministically with a stubbed global fetch.

conclusion: The v3 MetadataClient satisfies the contract: every failure is typed and normalized. Remote failures (business code != 0, non-2xx, or non-JSON bodies) are raised as TDAMError with code, message, requestId and optional normalized details; local validation failures are raised as ParamError before any request is sent. Neither path leaks a raw HTTP Response or a parsed-but-unvalidated {code,message,data} envelope. The executable contract at .prale-eval/validation/metadata-client.contract.ts drives the real sources and passes 24/24 checks (exit 0).
